newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower on Brazil imports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower on Brazil imports.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures collapsed on Wednesday and closed sharply lower amid news a U.S. firm had purchased 45,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans for import into the U.S., traders said.
"Brazil is on stream now, not just to Europe and the Pacific Rim but to us, too," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

Glencore Brazil said it sold 45,000 tonnes of soybeans to a U.S. firm, most likely for April or May shipment. U.S. exporters said the deal made economic sense because Brazilian soybeans were better quality and cheaper than U.S. supplies.

Traders said the news may have ended a two-month rally that took soybeans up more than $1 per bushel. While the market had accepted Brazil had ample soybean supplies, it hadn't counted on the beans making their way north.
"It's one thing for Brazil to be selling to China or Thailand or Vietnam," another trader said. "It's another when they're coming into U.S. markets.
Some traders said the sale proved U.S. soybeans were no longer competitive and prices would have to move lower.
Soybeans ended 29-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower with May off 27 at $8.28-1/2.

Soybeans were further weakened by news the Philippines passed on an overnight tender for U.S. soybeans. Manila also said it may shift to Brazilian supplies due to high U.S. prices. Last year, Manila bought most of its soybeans and soymeal from the United States.
Commodity funds began to liquidate massive long positions which spooked the market and prompted some panic selling. Traders said the pit had been bracing for the moment when funds pulled the plug.
Fund buying propelled soybeans to 8-1/2 year highs on Monday and was the catalyst for a two-month rally. Traders feared prices would quickly tumble below $8 per bushel if funds liquidated.
On the day, Refco Inc reportedly sold at least 11 million bushels May and five million July but bought six million May, including 1.5 million in the last minutes of trade.
Griffin Trading sold two million bushels May and Rosenthal Collins sold 2.5 million May and 1.5 million July.
In options, LIT reportedly sold 500 May $8.50 puts at 26 to 27 cents and SAK Futures sold 300 May $9.00 calls at 14 to 14-1/2 cents.
Technically, the May contract settled just above second support at 8.27-1/2 but closed well below the four-day moving averages.
